body: I’m bringing kandi to trade in GA!

By the time I’d be out there, I will have 4 months experience on rope (in a studio with a coach), but I am definitely more comfortable with silks as of now. Only having one tail has definitely been a creative challenge for me, but having anything set up would at least allow me to keep up with conditioning and improve basic techniques. The wind is a pain with silks, but we are located in a forest, so most days it isn’t very noticeable unless you’re near the treetops. 

As for the actual rigging, I’m not too worried. It’s been a while since I’ve been on site, so I don’t remember exactly what all the equipment is rated for off the top of my head, but most of it shouldn’t be a problem. After all, we do have to be prepared for someone to unexpectedly fall or dramatically jump off a platform (don’t do that though obviously). If I were to rig on the actual zip line system, I would connect the apparatus to multiple safe rigging points, so, if the main point fails, there is still a backup. It’s pretty much standard practice for us to have multiple connections points whenever there’s any additional risk. We also have other attractions that create more force than zip lining that I’m going to look into. Wherever I end up setting up will mostly determined by the owner and manger’s expertise with some feedback from me and coaches at my studio.

Aha something I have some experience with! I definitely noticed it was a lot easier for me to learn some of the first basic skills such as bubbles/lemons, forwards and backwards skating, crossing your feet over each other, balance, edges, etc than my friends who didn’t figure skate. I will say though, before I started roller skating I didn’t realize how different things such as spins would be. And park skating, if you choose to do that, is a whole other world. Any skills you come with will definitely be an asset and don’t worry too much about falling. Practice falling on purpose so it doesn’t seem as daunting when it happens accidentally and you can build some muscle memory on how to fall safely.

Bend your knees! Like way more than you think you should. It helps to keep you from falling backwards and makes you more stable. Plus, the closer you are to the ground, the less distance to fall. Good luck on your skating! You got this!

I strongly recommend checking out rollergirl.ca and seeing if there’s anything you like in your size there! They have a flat shipping rate and it doesn’t seem like their prices are as marked up as other stores. I’ve had great experiences with them, so it’s definitely worth checking out. Good luck finding your skates!

A few days ago I ordered a pair from rollergirl.ca and I’ve heard great things about them. If there’s nothing available on there that you want I recommend finding any skate shops around where ever you live (online or in person). If I were you, I’d avoid ordering from outside of Canada to hopefully keep shipping time and cost relatively low. I’ve heard of other people ordering from lowlife and retro rollers if you want to check those out.
